citations.name: requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.author_procedure
citations.commentary:
The context records the contents supplied in the prompt. The agent also has
tools for requesting additional contents, which are recorded when delivered.
Awaiting the ask builder returns the submitted `TestReview`; `verify` returns
a `Fingerprinted` containing the criterion's completed answer and the identity and
fingerprint of each input used during execution. Those fingerprints let the
application check when the answer may be stale.

{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission`
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validators.validate_node`
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.inputs`

rationale:
The passage is book commentary that cites `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.author_procedure` and, inside the fence, three more requirements. Each claim agrees with the cited declarations.

- **Recorded contents.** The passage says the context records the contents supplied in the prompt, and that tool-delivered contents are recorded when delivered. `author_procedure` says the context "combines delivered node contents, tool reads, direct inspection reads, and recorded edge selections into one dependency trace". It also says the context "records the node identities and fingerprints of the supplied contents".
- **Awaiting the ask builder.** The passage says awaiting it returns the submitted `TestReview`. This matches `judge.submission`: a successful call returns exactly one accepted submitted value, deserialized into `R`. `TestReview` is just the concrete `R` for this criterion.
- **`verify` and `Fingerprinted`.** The passage says `verify` returns a `Fingerprinted` with the completed answer and the identity and fingerprint of each input used. This matches `validate_node`, which says the completed answer and captured dependencies form the returned `Fingerprinted`. It also matches `inputs`, which gives `Fingerprinted` an `output()` and `dependencies()` of recorded node-content and successor-set observations.
- **Staleness.** The passage says the fingerprints let the application check when the answer may be stale. The cited text does not state this purpose in the same words. It follows from the recorded fingerprints, though, and the neighbouring requirements say the same: the `check_inputs` text in `evidence.md` and the fingerprinting text in `fingerprinting.md`. It does not contradict anything cited.

The passage uses `{cite}` for all four citations, which is the right role for explanatory prose. It carries no `{impl}` or `{test}` reference for any of them, so none is redundant.

text: :::{req} author_procedure
A `Criterion::execute` invocation receives one `Send + Sync`
`ValidationContext<'d, D>` for `D: Domain`, with tracked `inspection(&self)`
and the `ask(&self)` builder under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge`.
Each awaited ask builder runs its own conversation and returns its own submitted
answer. The context combines delivered node contents, tool reads, direct
inspection reads, and recorded edge selections into one dependency trace for
the criterion. It records the node identities and fingerprints of the supplied
contents. A later call that selects fewer nodes, or none, preserves earlier
inputs. An unawaited builder contributes no
agent-delivery dependencies.
Shared references support concurrent calls: builders, conversations, and
submission state remain independent, while updates to the trace are synchronized.
Calls can run concurrently without holding an exclusive context borrow across
an agent interaction or locking the whole context for the conversation.
The context is the same interface used by deterministic criteria under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation.criterion_trait`; its domain includes
evidence storage.
:::{req} judge.submission
The SDK derives the submission tool's JSON schema from `R` using `schemars`
and instructs the agent to finish through that tool. Its default name is
`submit_result` in the supplied `ToolAgent` harness. An application implementing
`Agent<D>` can supply its own submission name and acceptance rules, as described
in [Agent harness](agent-harness.md#adapt-an-existing-conversation).
A successful call returns exactly one accepted submitted value, deserialized
into `R`. Ordinary assistant text does not count. Ending without a valid
accepted submission returns an error. Provider failures and invalid terminal
submissions return `ValidationError::Agent`.
:::{req} validate_node
```rust,ignore
// Method on Validator<D>.
/// Execute the criterion and return its completed answer and observed inputs.
pub fn verify<V: Criterion<D>>(
&self,
criterion: V,
) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Fingerprinted<D, V::Ok>, ValidationError<D::Error>>> + Send;
Every call constructs a fresh `ValidationContext` identifying the source node
and calls `Criterion::execute` with that context. Its completed answer, including
a negative assessment, and captured dependencies form the returned `Fingerprinted`
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.inputs`.
:::{req} inputs
```rust,ignore
// Defined in habeas_sdk::graph.
/// A completed answer and the inputs used to produce it.
pub struct Fingerprinted<D: Domain, O> { /* private fields */ }
impl<D: Domain, O> Fingerprinted<D, O> {
/// The source node this answer concerns.
pub fn source_node_id(&self) -> &D::NodeId;
/// The question's path relative to that source.
pub fn criterion_path(&self) -> &CriterionPath;
/// The review rules used to produce this answer.
pub fn revision(&self) -> &str;
/// Recorded node-content and successor-set observations.
pub fn dependencies(&self) -> &[Dependency<D::NodeId, D::EdgeLabel>];
/// Borrow the completed answer.
pub fn output(&self) -> &O;
/// Take ownership of the completed answer.
pub fn into_output(self) -> O;
`verify` constructs this value from the criterion's completed answer and
execution trace. `load_evidence` reconstructs it from the selected saved record.
Its node identities and edge labels keep their domain-defined types.
